people.nameZh: 斯坦尼斯瓦夫·沃伊切霍夫斯基

body.zh-Hant: 斯坦尼斯瓦夫·沃伊切霍夫斯基1869年3月15日生於卡利什，家庭是家道中落的貴族。他在華沙大學求學時參加地下獨立活動，1892年被迫離開華沙，先後前往蘇黎世、巴黎與倫敦。他是波蘭社會黨的創建者之一，曾在維爾諾印製《工人報》，並與畢蘇斯基共同編輯這份報紙。1906年他回到華沙，著手組織波蘭的合作社。
body.en: Stanisław Wojciechowski was born on 15 March 1869 in Kalisz, into an impoverished noble family. While studying at the University of Warsaw he joined the underground independence movement; he was forced to leave Warsaw in 1892 and went to Zurich, Paris and London. He was one of the founders of the Polish Socialist Party, printed the paper Robotnik in Vilnius and co-edited it with Piłsudski. In 1906 he returned to Warsaw and began organising Polish cooperatives.

body.zh-Hant: 1919年1月起，他出任內政部長，並參與憲法的起草。波蘭國家記憶研究院把他的內政部長任期記為1919至1920年；1920年3月10日，他仍以內政部長身分在官方公報上簽署部令。論文作者指出，斯庫爾斯基內閣解散後，他決定辭去內政部長一職。
body.en: From January 1919 he served as Minister of the Interior and took part in drafting the constitution. The Institute of National Remembrance dates his ministry to 1919–1920, and on 10 March 1920 he still signed an ordinance in the official gazette as Minister of the Interior. A scholarly article notes that after the dissolution of Leopold Skulski's cabinet he decided to give up the post.

citations.quote: He was appointed Minister for the Interior in January 1919

body.zh-Hant: 在維托斯首屆內閣期間（1920年7月24日至1921年9月13日），沃伊切霍夫斯基主持總理府下的國家儲蓄事務委員會。他自述1921年3月17日憲法通過後加入人民黨「Piast」，這是他認為綱領最接近自己的政黨，並接受黨提議的黨週刊主編職務；《人民意志報》創刊號在1921年3月27日出版。
body.en: During Wincenty Witos's first cabinet (24 July 1920 to 13 September 1921), Wojciechowski chaired the Commission for State Savings attached to the Council of Ministers. In his memoirs he says he joined the People's Party "Piast" after the constitution was passed on 17 March 1921, regarding it as closest to his own programme, and he accepted the editorship of the party weekly; the first issue of Wola Ludu appeared on 27 March 1921.

citations.quote: Wojciechowski objął przewodnictwo Komisji dla spraw Oszczędności Państwowych

body.zh-Hant: 首任總統納魯托維奇於1922年12月16日遇刺後，國民議會選舉沃伊切霍夫斯基為總統。他對1924年幣制改革的法規內容有影響，也留意工業與合作社的發展。1926年5月政變中，他站在維托斯內閣一方，反對多年老友畢蘇斯基；5月14日他在政變後遞出辭呈。德國國家圖書館權威檔記他獲頒白鷹勳章與波蘭復興勳章（大十字）。
body.en: After President Gabriel Narutowicz was assassinated on 16 December 1922, the National Assembly elected Wojciechowski president. He influenced the content of the 1924 currency-reform decrees and paid attention to industry and the cooperative movement. In the May 1926 coup he sided with Witos's cabinet against his long-time friend Piłsudski, and he resigned on 14 May 1926 in the aftermath of the coup. The German National Library authority record lists him as a holder of the Order of the White Eagle and the Order of Polonia Restituta (Grand Cross).

body.zh-Hant: 辭職後，沃伊切霍夫斯基回到研究與教學，在高等商業學校（後來的華沙經濟學院）任教到1939年底。他在華沙起義期間的住宅被德軍縱火燒毀；他後來定居古翁波基，1953年4月9日在那裡幾乎被世人遺忘地去世，葬於波翁茲基公墓。德國國家圖書館權威檔也記下他的生卒日期。
body.en: After resigning he returned to research and teaching and taught at the Higher School of Commerce (later SGH) until the end of 1939. His house was deliberately set on fire by the Germans during the Warsaw Uprising. He later settled in Gołąbki, where he died almost completely forgotten on 9 April 1953, and was buried in the Powązki cemetery. The German National Library authority record also gives his birth and death dates.

body.zh-Hant: 亞歷山大（Alexander）生於1893年，德國國家圖書館權威檔與德意志傳記索引都把他的出生地記為塔托伊（Tatoi）。美國國會圖書館的名稱權威檔註明他是君士坦丁國王與蘇菲亞王后的次子，並收有希臘語轉寫形式Alexandros，與標準寫法「Alexander, King of Greece」並列。
body.en: Alexander was born in 1893; the German National Library authority record and the Deutsche Biographie index both give his birthplace as Tatoi. The Library of Congress name authority describes him as the second son of King Constantine and Queen Sophia and also records the transliterated form Alexandros alongside the standard heading "Alexander, King of Greece".

body.zh-Hant: 愛德華多·達托·伊拉迪耶（Eduardo Dato Iradier）1856年8月12日生於拉科魯尼亞，1921年3月8日卒於馬德里。西班牙眾議院網頁引用皇家歷史學院人物傳記辭典的開場介紹，稱他是法學家、政治人物，並是政府與保守黨的領袖（jefe）。德國國家圖書館權威檔把他的職業列為政治人物與法學家，並註明他曾任皇家法學與立法學院院長。
body.en: Eduardo Dato Iradier was born in A Coruña on 12 August 1856 and died in Madrid on 8 March 1921. The Spanish Congress web page quotes the opening description of the Royal Academy of History's biographical dictionary, which calls him a jurist, a politician, and chief of the Government and of the Conservative Party. The German National Library authority record lists his occupations as politician and jurist and notes that he presided over the Royal Academy of Jurisprudence and Legislation.

body.zh-Hant: 眾議院網頁說，達托進入政壇前已有自己興旺的律師事務所；他一生當過律師、多屆議員、眾議院議長、部長、內閣總理與馬德里市長，還是普拉多博物館理事會成員。他推動社會立法，贏得民眾好感，卻招來雇主與政界不少人的反感。
body.en: The Congress web page says that before entering politics Dato already ran a flourishing law practice of his own; over his life he was a lawyer, deputy on several occasions, President of the Congress, minister, President of the Council of Ministers, mayor of Madrid and a member of the Prado Museum board. His push for social legislation won him popular affection but the rejection of employers and large parts of political life.

body.zh-Hant: 1921年3月8日傍晚，達托離開參議院大樓、坐上自己的車。車開到獨立廣場時，一輛帶邊車的摩托車靠近並開槍；八發子彈穿透車身，五發擊中他的身體，他被送到附近布恩納維斯塔急救站時已經身亡。眾議院網頁說，他是不到三十年間第三位遇刺的內閣總理。
body.en: On the evening of 8 March 1921 Dato got into his car at the exit of the Senate building. When it reached the Plaza de la Independencia a motorcycle with a sidecar drew alongside and its occupants opened fire; eight bullets passed through the bodywork and five hit Dato, who was already dead when taken to the nearby Buenavista first-aid station. The Congress web page calls him the third President of the Council of Ministers killed in under three decades.

body.zh-Hant: 隔天眾議院全體集會，宣讀政府確認他死於「可恥暗殺」的通知，並暫停會議。1922年6月11日他的遺體被移到阿托查聖殿旁的偉人祠。馬德里法院在1923年10月11日的判決中認定馬特烏、尼科勞與卡薩內亞斯三人是兇手，三人被判死刑，之後減為無期徒刑。
body.en: The next day the Congress met in plenary, heard the Government's communication confirming that he had died as the victim of an "infamous assassination", and suspended its sittings. On 11 June 1922 his remains were moved to the Pantheon of Illustrious Men beside the Basilica of Atocha. In its ruling of 11 October 1923 the Madrid court held Mateu, Nicolau and Casanellas to be the killers; they were sentenced to death, commuted to life imprisonment.
